subject: Copywriting
title: The Question Slogan
description: Learn The Question Slogan in one minute.

hook.text: 'Got Milk?' 'Where's the Beef?' 'What's in Your Wallet?' Questions demand mental engagement.

buildup.text: Psychologists call it the 'instinctive elaboration' response.

discovery.text: Question slogans are interactive. The reader co-creates meaning by answering internally.

twist.text: Questions risk a wrong answer. 'Is Pepsi OK?' Diners answering 'No' reinforced a negative brand association for years.

climax.text: The best question slogans have only one answer—the brand.

punchline.text: Ask a question, own the answer. Questions engage the brain instantly.

quiz.question: Why do question slogans work so well?
options: The brain automatically seeks to answer questions

details.summary: Question slogans like 'Got Milk?' and 'Where's the Beef?' engage the brain by demanding an answer. An unanswered question creates cognitive tension — the Zeigarnik effect — that keeps the brand top of mind. Questions also invite participation, making the audience a co-creator of meaning.
details.whyItMatters: Questions are natural engagement hooks. A well-crafted question slogan turns passive viewers into active thinkers, dramatically increasing both recall and emotional investment.
takeaways: Questions create unresolved cognitive tension that boosts recall
The Zeigarnik effect keeps unanswered questions active in memory
Question slogans invite the audience to participate in meaning

faq.question: Why do question slogans stick in memory?
faq.answer: The brain treats unanswered questions as open loops that need closure. This is the Zeigarnik effect: incomplete tasks are remembered better than completed ones. 'Got Milk?' lingers because your brain keeps trying to answer it.

faq.question: What makes a good question slogan versus a weak one?
faq.answer: Good question slogans are short, provocative, and personally relevant. 'Got Milk?' works because everyone has experienced running out. Weak question slogans are rhetorical without consequence or too abstract to trigger a personal mental response.
